solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Devices for measuring radioactive element in green fruit

indicators.note: the radioactive element is placed in the middle of the fruit's letters

parts.note: gages are greengages, small green plums
U is the chemical symbol for uranium, a radioactive element

explanation.surface: Instruments for detecting radioactivity hidden in green fruit, like something from a food-safety lab.
explanation.definitionFit: Measuring instruments such as pressure or fuel dials are commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Pay the price, expressing no disagreement

definitions.meaning: to make amends or suffer for a wrong done
split into two words, the phrase for being in complete harmony with someone

explanation.surface: Someone who accepts a penalty without arguing about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to pay for a wrong; split in two, the word becomes the phrase for being in full agreement.

clue.text: Printer has begun Roget in new format, missing nothing out

indicators.note: putting the letters into a new layout means they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: missing signals that a letter is dropped from the thesaurus name
out confirms the letter for nothing is removed from Roget

parts.note: taken as written, the compiler of the thesaurus
O is the zero shape, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A printing firm reissuing Roget's Thesaurus in a new edition, with nothing left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing ... out' drops the O from ROGET to leave RGET; 'in new format' rearranges BEGUN with RGET.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Gutenberg, the fifteenth-century German pioneer of movable type, is the most famous printer in history.

clue.text: Chartist looks happy

definitions.meaning: the Victorian author of Self-Help, who campaigned for parliamentary reform with Chartist aims

explanation.surface: A political campaigner who seems pleased with how things are going.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a nineteenth-century British movement for working men's voting rights; Samuel Smiles was secretary of a Leeds reform body sharing their aims.
explanation.definitionFit: A person grinning broadly beams; the surname belongs to a reformer allied with that working-class movement.

clue.text: Shabby old magistrate, a leftie

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of old Venice or Genoa
a red is a left-winger or communist

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a scruffy, left-wing old judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pages with turned-down corners look worn, so the word has come to mean worn and shabby generally.

clue.text: Sadly undone by limited provision of insurance policy

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or in a sorry state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A disappointed policyholder ruined by a stingy payout from the insurer.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is every letter of UNDONE BY LIMITED, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a clause in life or accident cover paying twice the sum in certain cases, such as accidental death.

clue.text: Primate sounding cheerless on recording

indicators.note: sounding means the words are spoken and the result is what is heard

parts.note: cheerless is grey and a recording is a tape, so grey on tape, said quickly, is what is heard

explanation.surface: A monkey or ape heard sounding glum on a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' turns GREY TAPE, said quickly, into a near match for the two-word animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas, chimpanzees and orangutans are large primates grouped together under this name.

clue.text: Van Gogh regularly starts to retreat, obviously disturbing behaviour

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the painter's name
the starts of the next two words give their first letters

explanation.surface: The painter Van Gogh's erratic conduct, before he retreats, is plainly troubling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes A, G, G from VAN GOGH; 'starts to' gives R and O.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for aggressive, troublemaking conduct, short for aggravation.

clue.text: Greece isn't working — protesters ultimately coming out animated

indicators.note: working signals the letters are being set in motion and rearranged
coming out says a letter leaves the fodder
ultimately points to the final letter of protesters

explanation.surface: A news report on Greece's economic woes, with protesters finally leaving the streets in a lively mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives S, which 'coming out' removes from GREECE ISN'T to leave GREECEINT; 'working' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone animated is full of vigour and lively, a close synonym.

clue.text: Present image, but not one to get acclaim

indicators.note: but not says the following item is excluded from the image word

parts.note: an icon is an image, especially a religious one
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tribute is praise or acclaim

explanation.surface: A donated portrait offered in hope of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' is the verb, to give as one's share, not the noun or adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To present a gift or donation is to give it, the same as chipping in.

clue.text: Maybe Irishman in a storm, half confused

indicators.note: only half of the storm word is jumbled, its second half swapped round

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind or storm

explanation.surface: An Irishman caught in a storm, half bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half confused' swaps only the last two letters of GALE, LE becoming EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Celt of Ireland or the Scottish Highlands is so called; 'Maybe' warns that a Scot also qualifies.

clue.text: Miserly at first, you and I will have good intentions

indicators.note: at first places the stingy word ahead of the rest

parts.note: mean means stingy or miserly
you and I will contracts to we'll, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A stingy start, but the couple promise they'll do the right thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone whose motives are kind even if results fall short.

clue.text: Difficult having little King in manger

indicators.note: having means the hard word holds something
in confirms the king's letter goes inside

parts.note: tough means difficult
R, short for rex, Latin for king, is a little or abbreviated king

explanation.surface: A tricky nativity scene with the infant King in the manger.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is a feeding box for animals, essentially an open trough holding fodder.

clue.text: Old horse half visible in architectural feature

indicators.note: only half of the childish horse word can be seen

parts.note: gee-gee is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: An ancient horse half shown in a carving on a building.
explanation.walkthrough: GEE-GEE is British nursery talk for a horse; half of it gives GEE.
explanation.definitionFit: An S-shaped moulding or pointed arch is a classic decorative element in buildings.

clue.text: Boy guarded by soldier on list, upcoming fighter

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
the boy is protected on both sides by the soldier

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a lad is a boy

indicators.note: in a down clue upcoming means the list reads upward, backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A young man escorted by a soldier, listed as a future fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Roman arenas staged armed combatants who fought for public entertainment.

clue.text: Trouble-maker having nothing, half-educated, loutish

parts.note: an imp is a mischief-maker
O is the zero shape, meaning nothing
literary has the sense of educated or well read; its first half is lite

explanation.surface: A barely schooled troublemaker with no manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-educated' is half of LITERARY, i.e. LITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude, uncouth behaviour is the hallmark of a lout, so the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: 'Flexible friend' gets millions spent — in such a manner?

indicators.note: spent means used up and gone, so the money letter disappears

parts.note: limber means supple or flexible
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A credit card being used to blow millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flexible friend' was the advertising slogan of Access, a British credit card. 'spent' removes M from LIMBERALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending millions on a credit card is spending lavishly and freely, the manner the question mark points to.

clue.text: After concert I understand someone I must oblige?

indicators.note: after places the rest following the concert word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
to see is to understand

explanation.surface: Following a concert, someone realises they owe another person a favour.
explanation.definitionFit: The person to whom a pledge is made is owed its fulfilment, so the pledger must oblige them.

clue.text: Wicked greed somehow makes one troubled

parts.note: bad means wicked

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Wicked greed somehow leaves a person troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pestered and harassed repeatedly leaves one troubled, as a hunted badger is.

clue.text: Player returned from injury?

definitions.meaning: a defender in football, rugby or hockey
a player who has recovered is said to be on the pitch again

explanation.surface: A sportsman fit again after time out hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Full-back and half-back are field positions; a player who has recovered is said to be in the team again.

clue.text: Shelter unknown character found in a poor part of town

indicators.note: the unknown is found within the poor district

parts.note: a slum is a poor, run-down district
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A refuge for a mysterious stranger in a deprived neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuge or protection, as granted to a refugee, is the core sense of the word.

clue.text: Funny show with model beginning to caress old male

parts.note: to sit is to pose as an artist's model

indicators.note: the beginning of caress is its first letter

parts.note: OM is short for old man

explanation.surface: A comedy with a model caressing an old man.
explanation.definitionFit: Situation comedy is a humorous television genre, a funny show by definition.

clue.text: Participating in democracy, nice diplomatic type

indicators.note: participating in means the answer takes part inside the words that follow, its letters running across them

explanation.surface: A smooth envoy taking part in democratic life and being pleasant about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue first published was for RUNIC (RU, rugby union, plus NIC(e)) and cannot give this answer; the corrected clue is used here.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat who expects the worst of everyone may be a doubter of motives, so the definition is a loose, mischievous one.

clue.text: Parsimonious person before rendering penitential psalm

parts.note: a miser hoards money
ere is an old word meaning before

explanation.surface: A stingy person sings a hymn of repentance.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalm 51, beginning 'Have mercy' in Latin, is the best known of the penitential psalms.

clue.text: Designation for Victoria, set to be a star

parts.note: RI, Regina Imperatrix, queen and empress, was Victoria's royal designation
to gel is to set firm

explanation.surface: A girl called Victoria destined for stardom.
explanation.definitionFit: The bright blue-white supergiant in Orion is a named star.

clue.text: Do well in life without good school

indicators.note: without means the good letter is left off

parts.note: to get on is to succeed in life

explanation.surface: Doing well in life without a good school education.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word; the school is Eton College, England's famous public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College near Windsor is England's best-known private boarding school.

clue.text: Irish stick, possibly illegal, used by husband? Keep quiet about that

indicators.note: the quiet word goes about, around, the rest

parts.note: sh is a call to keep quiet

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: An Irish cudgel, perhaps unlawful, wielded by a husband who wants it hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram and 'about' the wrapping; 'Keep quiet about that' reads like a plea for secrecy but is the outer shell of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional Irish wooden club or walking stick, often of blackthorn.

clue.text: Kitchen stuff about to be brought to part of garden

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
a rockery is a garden bed of stones and plants

explanation.surface: Kitchen items about to be moved out to the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates, cups and dishes are kitchen items collectively known by this word.

clue.text: Short-lived insect won't necessarily take off

definitions.meaning: an insect whose adult life lasts only a day or so
read as two words, something that might or might not fly

explanation.surface: A doubtful prospect for flight, like an uncertain plane.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is famous for its brief adult life; split in two, the word says flight is only possible.
